problem_type: hardcoded three-value union type blocks any MCP stdio tool from being a first-class client
symptom: Only Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can be signed and trusted as MCP clients. Any other AI tool (WorkBuddy, AutoClaw, etc.) that speaks MCP stdio must connect as 'external', gaining no identity binding and no trusted-host privilege, even if the user explicitly wants to grant it.
direct_cause: AuthenticatedMcpClient was a three-value union type literal in security.ts, MCP_CLIENTS was a hardcoded Set, and TRUSTED_HOSTS was a hardcoded Set of four values. All downstream consumers checked membership in these sets, making it structurally impossible to add new clients without code changes.
class_root: Identity and trust were modeled as an exhaustive enumeration instead of a validated-string registry, violating P4 (generic-first). The HMAC signing mechanism was already fully generic (HMAC(token, 'nomi-mcp-client:v1:<client>')) — only the type annotation and membership checks were restrictive.
affected_population: Users of any MCP stdio AI tool other than Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor
Third-party MCP client developers who want first-class Nomi integration
entry_points: MCP stdio initialize frame with unrecognized clientInfo.name
User attempts to register a non-builtin tool in Automation settings
signMcpClient() called with a custom key string
normalizeAutomationPolicySettings() with a custom client key in trustedHosts
invariants: HMAC signing mechanism is unchanged: signMcpClient(key) = HMAC-SHA256(token, 'nomi-mcp-client:v1:' + key). No exemption from proof verification for any client, builtin or custom.
Custom clients gain identity (trusted-host privilege) ONLY when the user explicitly adds them to trustedHosts — there is no automatic escalation.
Builtin client keys (claude, codex, cursor) cannot be overridden by a custom profile registration.
RPC server still only listens on 127.0.0.1 — no network surface change.
A key with invalid format (uppercase, spaces, special chars) is always rejected by isValidMcpClientKey() and produces null from signMcpClient().
External clients (unrecognized name, no valid proof) remain 'external' with no trusted-host authority.
Self-declared names in MCP initialize.clientInfo are audit labels only — HMAC proof is what grants identity.
migration: Purely additive. Existing builtin clients retain identical behavior. AuthenticatedMcpClient widened from union to string is backward-compatible: all valid builtin strings still pass isValidMcpClientKey(). Custom profiles file defaults absent (treated as empty list).
residual_risks: UI for adding/managing custom profiles is deferred (TODO in AutomationPermissionsSection.tsx and ConnectAssistantCard) — users cannot yet configure custom profiles via the GUI, only via direct file edit or future UI.
watchFile polling (1s interval) may miss rapid successive writes in pathological test environments, but is stable for the 'user saves settings' use case.
ui_todo: CustomMcpClientCard component not yet implemented. See TODO comment in src/workbench/settings/AutomationPermissionsSection.tsx. Requires design mockup approval (R8) before implementation.
